newsitem.title: USA: Ill. Governor Jim Edgar gets high marks in poll.
newsitem.headline: Ill. Governor Jim Edgar gets high marks in poll.

text.p: Illinois Gov. Jim Edgar won high approval ratings from voters who were split on whether the popular Republican should run for a Democratic-held U.S. Senate seat, a poll published Monday said.

The Chicago Tribune poll of 711 likely voters found 68 percent approved of the job Edgar has done during nearly two four-year terms as governor, while 23 percent disapproved and 8 percent were unsure.

Edgar failed to push through a statewide 25 percent tax increase earlier this year designed to raise money for public schools while providing property tax relief, a program favored by his Democratic opponent in 1994. The policy failure did not hurt Edgar among survey respondents, but he was seen as not explaining the plan well enough.

Edgar, who has recovered from heart bypass surgery, is considering his options for 1998, which include running for re-election, campaigning for Democratic Sen. Carol Moseley-Braun's seat, or retiring from politics.
Asked what Edgar should do, 29 percent of those surveyed said he should run for governor again, 28 percent said he should run for the U.S. Senate, and 43 percent did not know.
Moseley-Braun, the first black woman elected to the Senate, received poor approval ratings in the Tribune poll, which had an error margin of plus or minus 4 percent.
